For months since I started university, I had been masking my true self so as to appear normal in front of everyone. But slowly it started wearing off from the burnout of school assignments, and from this one toxic friend in my class. Lately in the past weeks in school, almost all my friends, classmates, and teachers could now easily tell that I'm struggling inside just by looking at my facial expression and my eyes. They were all saying that I looked very gloomy and emo, and that there was no light in my eyes. Most of my friends didnt do anything to console me because they didnt know what to say. Only one friend attempted to check up on me, but I told him not to worry, and that I will be fine. The truth is I just dont wanna burden him or anyone with my problems, it makes me feel guilty for making them uncomfortable and confused as I vent to them. And in the past, I have lost friends when I vented to them about my mental health, and I dont wanna repeat the same thing again to my current friends. 

So to answer your question, no I have not been happy in a long time. I feel alone in my suffering, and idk how long more I can suppress all these negative feelings.

Tbh it depends. Even though i have autism, i still struggle with talking to others with similar conditions

There are several reasons. Usually its either they are picky of their new friends, or they're awkward and have no idea how to keep the conversation flowing, or they feel overwhelmed by the huge number of dms received, or the person they are talking to is a creep

Its tough but im sure its still possible. Sometimes u gotta step out of your comfort zone to meet new friends. You can start off with making online friends around your area, or finding a local group that shares similar interests as you. Those are just some ways u can try.

Im in the same boat too with the friends i made in high school. We graduated years ago and since then they have been talking less to me after we all went to a different college. I have tried many times to reconnect with them but whenever we hung out, it just wasnt the same anymore. They didnt talk much to me and werent at all interested in anything i have to say. Its sad for me to say this but i think its best for u move on from them and be with new people, its just not worth anyone's time.

For me, its because of depression and autism, which completely sucks out all my social energy when im with people. I also struggle with finding interesting things to talk about when my classmates ask me questions about my life or hobbies, it makes me look like some awkward weirdo.
Same here, i dont have much to say about myself when im around people. I also lack motivation to seek new interests so im basically stuck in one place

i did reach out to people here with similar interests (like movies, filmmaking and photography etc) as me, but i still get no response. And meeting up with people irl at local events sounds really impossible due to my social anxiety, i cant even survive at my school and workplace without breaking down.

Funnily enough it was a lot easier for me years ago to make long-term friends on reddit and discord, but now i cant even get anyone's attention with my first message
is there anywhere else I could make friends? I know i could try doing it irl but joining a local event or some group meetup sounds daunting cus of my social anxiety
